title: The dynamics of RAD51 foci formation and elongation in living human cells.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched both Zenodo records named in the data availability statement (16621349 concept DOI -> v2.1 record 21910069, and v2.0 record 20677613) and listed their files via the Zenodo API: a single 465,563-byte ZIP of ImageJ macros, Groovy scripts, two plugin JARs and Labkit pixel classifiers, licence GPL-3.0, resource type 'Software'. Listed the matching GitHub repository (19 entries: 15 scripts/JARs/README/LICENSE plus one 'Labkit classifiers' folder) - no images, no measurement tables, no example data. Searched BioStudies/BioImage Archive for 'MND1 RAD51 homology search' and 'Friskes' - no image deposition for this study. Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out (75 s hard deadline) on the one attempt allowed, so the NAR supplement listing is not retrievable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That RAD51 focus area and total skeleton length were measured with Ilastik v1.3.2 pixel plus object classification, that GFP-MND1 structures were segmented with a Labkit classifier and tracked with TrackMate after StarDist nucleus segmentation, and that replicate counts are mostly N = 3. No per-cell or per-focus numbers were verifiable because no quantification table is deposited; the statement ends 'Any additional information required to reanalyze the data reported in this paper is available from the lead contact upon request.'

a1_downloadable.note: The only public deposit is 465 KB of analysis code and Labkit pixel classifiers (Zenodo 21910069, GPL-3.0, type 'Software'). No microscopy images and no quantification tables are deposited anywhere I could find; the data availability statement routes everything else to 'the lead contact upon request', which is an explicit A1 fail.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table at all, so no label column. The quantities the paper models (focus area, skeleton length, topology class, time to resolution) would have to be regenerated from images that are not public.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs would be 3D live-cell confocal/AiryScan time-lapse stacks of GFP-MND1 and RAD51; none are available, only the scripts that would process them.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clear in the methods (micrometres for skeleton length and area, hours after irradiation, Gy of ionising radiation) - but there are no files carrying them.

a5_enough_rows.note: No row count could be verified. The paper reports N = 3 biological replicates for most panels; per-cell and per-focus counts appear only inside figure panels, far from the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Nothing to size: the deposited archive is 0.5 MB. Had the raw 3D time-lapse images been released they would likely be tens to hundreds of gigabytes and need a GPU for segmentation.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked - there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The labels in this paper are themselves model outputs: focus topology percentages come from the authors' own Ilastik object classifier and the GFP-MND1 masks from a Labkit pixel classifier (whose own README warns 'These will probably not work on your own data'). Training on them would distil those classifiers, not learn biology.

c2_audit.note: Not searched: the evaluation stopped at the A1 failure. The empty list does not mean no models exist - deep-learning foci segmentation and tracking (StarDist, Cellpose, TrackMate, Ilastik) is in fact a busy area.

backbone.name: Cellpose/StarDist-style segmentation backbone (would apply to foci segmentation if images existed)
backbone.licence: not assessed; deposited code is GPL-3.0

integration.partner_dataset: Not assessed (BioImage Archive / Image Data Resource would be the natural partner if images were deposited)

plain_idea.one_liner: Use live-cell microscopy movies of repair-protein spots to predict which spots stretch out and when they disappear
plain_idea.train_on: Would have trained on 3D time-lapse fluorescence movies of human cells after irradiation, one example per tracked RAD51/MND1 focus (a bright spot of DNA-repair protein). Number of examples: unknown - no movies or tables are public.
plain_idea.predict: Would have predicted the shape class of a focus (round versus elongated) and how long it takes to disappear. The true answer comes from the authors' Ilastik and Labkit image classifiers applied to the same movies, not from an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying homologous recombination (the error-free DNA break repair pathway) currently score these structures by hand or with hand-trained classifiers; an automatic, transferable scorer would make DNA-repair screens comparable between labs. As posed here it cannot be attempted, because neither the images nor the measurements are public.

ml_idea: Considered: segment and classify DNA-repair foci in live-cell movies (round versus elongated RAD51/MND1 structures) and predict time-to-resolution per focus, with genetic perturbations (RAD54L loss, cohesin loss) as held-out conditions. Dead on arrival: only the ImageJ/Groovy scripts and Labkit classifiers are deposited (465 KB, GPL-3.0); the images and the per-focus measurement tables are 'available from the lead contact upon request', and the only labels that exist are the output of the authors' own classifiers.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated - no data to size. The 465 KB code archive was the only download.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done in two API calls: list the files in the Zenodo record. It returns one 465 KB ZIP of type 'Software' and nothing else, so there is no feature/label table to build.

verdict_reason: A1, A2, A3, A5, A7 and A8 all fail: the only public deposit is 465 KB of ImageJ analysis scripts and Labkit pixel classifiers (verified via the Zenodo API and the GitHub listing), no microscopy images or quantification tables are deposited in Zenodo, BioImage Archive or elsewhere I could find, and the paper routes the rest to the lead contact on request. Even if the measurements were released, the labels are the output of the authors' own Ilastik/Labkit classifiers, so a model would distil those classifiers rather than learn biology.
